info.title: Asset Tracker API
info.description: Terminal, kit and contract inventory, the Equipment Catalog with its waveform, service, transport and platform libraries, the joint compatibility matrix, the nets library and the PACE planner. Every route requires authentication except the CSV import templates, which carry no user data.

get.description: Returns the whole card in one read: the header plus both channel wheels, with each channel's frequency already resolved (override where set, the net's own otherwise). parameters.name: theater
parameters.description: Which of the squadron's two cards. Every squadron keeps one whole card per theater; conus when omitted. An unknown value is refused with PACE_INVALID_THEATER.

400.description: An unknown theater (PACE_INVALID_THEATER)

put.description: Replaces the card in one transaction. An upsert, not a create: the editor is one page with one Save and a squadron always has exactly one card, so this returns 200 whether a card existed or not. A radio omitted from `plans` is left untouched; a radio present with an empty `channels` list clears that wheel. Requires admin, editor, rto, or planner. Responds with the saved card, re-read from the database. Every row carries its own `highlights` list naming the fields that print as changed, and the header carries a free-text `version`; an unknown mark name is refused with `PACE_INVALID_HIGHLIGHT`.

parameters.name: section

get.summary: Export a squadron's PACE channels as CSV
get.description: Streams one squadron's assigned wheel positions as CSV, one row per assigned position across both wheels and both theaters, CONUS rows first; the theater column says which card a row came from. Export-only: a channel row is meaningless without a plan and a net that already exist, so there is no template and no import. Section is required rather than optional - a card belongs to a squadron and there is no all-squadrons card to export. Any existing section key is accepted; a squadron with nothing saved yet exports a header row and no data rows, matching the empty scaffold GET /pace/{section} returns. Read-only; open to any authenticated user.

post.summary: Export several datasets as one zip
post.description: Renders several datasets in one request and returns a zip holding one CSV export per dataset. Each dataset carries its own column selection and its own filters, named exactly as that dataset's single-export query parameters. POST rather than GET because a fully-expanded nine-dataset column selection runs past a thousand characters before any filter, and the request head has to carry that alongside an Entra token - going over surfaces as a connection failure rather than a clean 4xx. Entries are named exactly as the equivalent single-dataset route names its download, and appear in alphabetical order by resource, which is the registry order set by csvregistry.Exporters rather than the order the datasets were requested, so the same selection always produces the same bytes. There is no second rendering path: each entry calls the same service method the single-dataset route calls. No partial success - a failure anywhere fails the whole request, because a truncated archive delivered with a 200 hides what is missing. The response is always a zip, including when a single dataset is requested; the app never sends one dataset here, because planCsvRequest routes a lone selection to that dataset's own GET route so an existing single-dataset export keeps producing the byte-identical file it always did. Read-only; open to any authenticated user, which is what every single-dataset export carries.

200.description: Zip archive returned, one CSV per requested dataset

400.description: Invalid body, unknown resource, duplicate resource, or a section-scoped dataset with no section

404.description: A section-scoped dataset named a section that does not exist

500.description: The archive could not be built

post.summary: Download several import templates as one zip
post.description: Renders several datasets in one request and returns a zip holding one import template per dataset. A template has no rows, so the per-dataset filters do not apply here and only the column selection does. An export-only dataset, meaning contracts and pace-channels, is rejected with CSV_BUNDLE_NO_TEMPLATE rather than silently omitted. POST rather than GET because a fully-expanded nine-dataset column selection runs past a thousand characters before any filter, and the request head has to carry that alongside an Entra token - going over surfaces as a connection failure rather than a clean 4xx. Entries are named exactly as the equivalent single-dataset route names its download, and appear in alphabetical order by resource, which is the registry order set by csvregistry.Exporters rather than the order the datasets were requested, so the same selection always produces the same bytes. There is no second rendering path: each entry calls the same service method the single-dataset route calls. No partial success - a failure anywhere fails the whole request, because a truncated archive delivered with a 200 hides what is missing. The response is always a zip, including when a single dataset is requested; the app never sends one dataset here, because planCsvRequest routes a lone selection to that dataset's own GET route so an existing single-dataset export keeps producing the byte-identical file it always did. Unlike the nine single-dataset template routes, this one is authenticated: those are open because a template path is a plain link a user may have bookmarked, and a POST carrying a dataset selection is not a bookmarkable link.

200.description: Zip archive returned, one CSV template per requested dataset

400.description: Invalid body, unknown resource, duplicate resource, an export-only dataset with no template, or a section-scoped dataset with no section

404.description: A section-scoped dataset named a section that does not exist

500.description: The archive could not be built

PaceHighlights.description: The fields of this one row that print as changed (red on the card, the print sheet and both exports). Names come from the row's own list in pace/model.go: header title, date, version; plan label; channel net, tx, rx; LTAC and TACSAT row name, channel, up, down, sat, crypto; TMN row label, value; tier name, service, detail. An unknown name is a 400 with code PACE_INVALID_HIGHLIGHT naming the row. A repeat is de-duplicated on write. In a response this is always an array, never null.

PaceFreqRowResponse.description: One printed line of the LTAC or TACSAT table. `up` and `down` are the sheet's column headings; the columns behind them are up_freq and down_freq.

PaceTmnRowResponse.description: One line of the TACTICAL MISSION NETWORK box.

PaceTierResponse.description: One PACE tile, with its references already resolved. The equipment nomenclature, nickname, photo and service rates are joined in by the repository so the sheet renders from one payload.

source.description: Which reference field matters: equipment, transport, custom or none

equipment_nickname.description: The catalog nickname the tile titles itself with. Empty for a record that has none; the client falls back to the nomenclature.

service_cir.description: Empty when the tier has no equipment or no matching service on it. Always empty for a radio.

SavePaceFreqRowInput.description: One line of the LTAC or TACSAT table. Which block it belongs to is the array it arrives in, and its position is that array's order, so neither is a field the client sends.

SavePaceTmnRowInput.description: One line of the TACTICAL MISSION NETWORK box.

SavePaceTierInput.description: One PACE tile. Which reference field matters is decided by `source`; the others are cleared on write rather than trusted.

PaceChannelResponse.description: One net on one wheel position. The frequency is already resolved - the per-channel override where set, the net's own otherwise - so no consumer has to re-implement that precedence.

label_override.description: Caption shown in place of the net's name. Empty means use the net's name.

is_overridden.description: True when a tx, rx, or unit override is set, so the editor can show that the departure from the net's own values is deliberate.

PacePlanResponse.description: One wheel: a squadron's channel assignments for one radio. Only assigned channels appear in `channels`; a consumer renders 1..channel_count and fills the gaps with the unassigned placeholder.

id.description: Plan ID. Empty for a wheel the squadron has not configured yet, which is scaffolded rather than omitted.

radio_type.description: The radio this wheel is for

label.description: Free-text caption rendered beneath the wheel. Empty renders no caption at all.

channel_count.description: Number of positions on the wheel

updated_by.description: Name of the last user to save this wheel

updated_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the last save. Empty for a wheel the squadron has not configured yet.

channels.description: Assigned positions only, ordered by channel_number

theater.description: Which of the squadron's two cards this is

title.description: Centred on the sheet. Names the exercise or operation the card is for.

effective_date.description: Date the card takes effect, as YYYY-MM-DD. Empty when unset, and the sheet then shows no date subtext.

plans.description: Always both radios, JEM then MPU5. A radio the squadron has not configured is scaffolded empty with the default 16 channels rather than omitted, so no consumer has to special-case "not set up yet".

emblem_url.description: Empty when the squadron has uploaded no emblem, which is the sheet's signal to draw its generated placeholder instead.

version.description: Free text printed after the effective date, exactly as typed (`v2`). Empty prints nothing.

tiers.description: Always exactly four, in P A C E order, even for a squadron that has saved none.

channel_number.description: Wheel position, 1-based. Must not exceed the plan's channel_count, and must not repeat within one plan.

net_id.description: ID of a net that must exist, belong to this same squadron, and be carried by this radio - a net of radio_type 'both' belongs on either wheel, anything else must match.

tx_freq_override.description: Transmit frequency for this position only. Empty uses the net's own.

rx_freq_override.description: Receive frequency for this position only. Empty uses the net's own.

freq_unit_override.description: Frequency unit for this position only. Empty uses the net's own.

label_override.description: Caption shown in place of the net's name

label.description: Free-text caption rendered beneath the wheel

channel_count.description: Number of positions on the wheel. Omitted or 0 defaults to 16.

channels.description: Assigned positions only. An empty list clears every assignment on this wheel.

SavePaceCardRequest.description: The whole comms card in one payload. The editor is one page with one Save, so the write surface is a whole-card replace rather than granular per-channel endpoints. A radio omitted from `plans` is left untouched; a radio present with an empty `channels` list clears that wheel.

title.description: Centred on the sheet. Names the exercise or operation the card is for.

effective_date.description: Date the card takes effect, as YYYY-MM-DD. An empty string clears it, which is how the editor's "Include date" checkbox turns the subtext off.

plans.description: The wheels this save touches. Capped at the number of radios a card has, since a repeat is refused as a duplicate radio: one save is one transaction, and an oversized payload would hold the write lock long enough to stall every other squadron's save.

version.description: Free text printed after the effective date (`v2`). Empty prints nothing.

ltac_rows.description: The sheet's LTAC table. The cap is the number of lines the band has room for on the fixed page; past it the PACE tiles are pushed off the paper, so an over-long list is a 400 rather than a silent truncation.

tacsat_rows.description: The sheet's TACSAT table. Same cap rule as ltac_rows.

tmn_rows.description: The TACTICAL MISSION NETWORK box. Same cap rule as ltac_rows.

tiers.description: The four PACE tiles. Absent entirely means unchanged, which is what lets an older client keep saving channel edits without wiping tiers it never knew about. Present means replace all four.

total.description: Entries carried by at least one asset, not the library size.

PlatformResponse.description: An external comms platform. Its waveform set lives in one row: no join table.

category.description: The branch or branches operating the platform. Closed list: USA, USMC, USN, USAF, USSF, USCG, OGA (other government agency). Branch names such as "Air Force" and any case are accepted; stored as abbreviations, deduplicated, in that order of precedence. Anything else is refused with PLATFORM_INVALID_CATEGORY. Empty means no branch set.

type.description: Closed list. Case, surrounding space, repeated spaces and underscores are normalised; anything else is refused with PLATFORM_INVALID_TYPE. Blank on create becomes aircraft.

waveform_abbrevs.description: Waveforms declared on the platform directly. Each must exist in the waveform library; de-duplicated case-insensitively, keeping the first spelling.

equipment_ids.description: Catalog radios it carries, where known. An id naming a deleted record is kept and ignored by the matrix.

CreatePlatformRequest.description: Uniqueness is case-insensitive on designation. An abbrev the waveform library does not declare is refused with PLATFORM_UNKNOWN_WAVEFORM.

category.description: The branch or branches operating the platform. Closed list: USA, USMC, USN, USAF, USSF, USCG, OGA (other government agency). Branch names such as "Air Force" and any case are accepted; stored as abbreviations, deduplicated, in that order of precedence. Anything else is refused with PLATFORM_INVALID_CATEGORY. Empty means no branch set.

type.description: Closed list. Case, surrounding space, repeated spaces and underscores are normalised; anything else is refused with PLATFORM_INVALID_TYPE. Blank on create becomes aircraft.

UpdatePlatformRequest.description: PATCH is a partial update: an omitted field is left as it is, which is why every property here is optional. A present waveform_abbrevs replaces the whole set.

category.description: The branch or branches operating the platform. Closed list: USA, USMC, USN, USAF, USSF, USCG, OGA (other government agency). Branch names such as "Air Force" and any case are accepted; stored as abbreviations, deduplicated, in that order of precedence. Anything else is refused with PLATFORM_INVALID_CATEGORY. Empty means no branch set.

type.description: Closed list. Case, surrounding space, repeated spaces and underscores are normalised; anything else is refused with PLATFORM_INVALID_TYPE. Blank on create becomes aircraft.

OrganizationResponse.description: A participant an operation can check in. The key is the identity and never changes.

key.description: Lowercase slug: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with an underscore.

branch.description: One of USA, USMC, USN, USAF, USSF, USCG, OGA, or empty when the organization is not a service component.

section_key.description: The squadron this organization maps to, or empty. A section maps to at most one organization.

operation_count.description: How many distinct operations have this organization checked in, computed on read. Ad hoc participants count for nothing. While it is above 0, a delete is refused with ORGANIZATION_IN_USE.

CreateOrganizationRequest.description: The key is normalised to lowercase and must be unused. A section_key must name an existing section.

branch.description: Branch names such as "Army" and any case are accepted and stored as the abbreviation. Blank means not a service component. Anything else is refused with ORGANIZATION_INVALID_BRANCH.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description: PATCH is a partial update: an omitted field is left as it is. A blank branch or section_key clears it.

branch.description: Branch names such as "Army" and any case are accepted and stored as the abbreviation. Blank means not a service component. Anything else is refused with ORGANIZATION_INVALID_BRANCH.

OperationResponse.description: A named effort organizations check in to.

acronym.description: Optional; stored upper-case so the operation can show as "Operation XXX". Blank for none.

start_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or empty when not set.

end_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or empty when not set. Never before start_date.

participant_count.description: How many organizations are checked in.

open_rfi_count.description: How many RFIs on the operation are still open.

OrganizationSummary.description: The slice of an organization a check-in displays, joined in on read.

adhoc.description: True for an "Other" organization that exists only on this check-in; its key is then empty.

ParticipantResponse.description: One organization's check-in to one operation.

equipment_ids.description: Catalog record ids, satcom and radio. An id naming a deleted record is kept.

platform_ids.description: Platform Library ids the participant brings (airframe, UAV, ship, vehicle, ground station), declared before its radios. De-duplicated. An id naming a deleted platform is kept.

waveform_abbrevs.description: Each must exist in the waveform library.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339. Echo it back as expected_updated_at to guard a save.

asset_phases.description: Each asset the participant brings (platform, catalog record or transport id) mapped to the ids of the phases it is present in, in phase order. An asset in no phase maps to an empty list. Never null.

phases.description: The operation's phases in order. Never null.

sites.description: The operation's sites (locations) in order. Never null.

CreateOperationRequest.description: Uniqueness is case-insensitive on name. A blank status means planning.

acronym.description: Optional; stored upper-case so the operation can show as "Operation XXX". Blank for none.

UpdateOperationRequest.description: PATCH is a partial update: an omitted field is left as it is. A blank start_date or end_date clears it.

acronym.description: Optional; stored upper-case. A blank value clears it.

SaveParticipantRequest.description: Replaces the whole check-in: all four lists and the contact fields are stored as sent, so an omitted list becomes empty. An abbrev the waveform library does not declare is refused with PARTICIPANT_UNKNOWN_WAVEFORM.

platform_ids.description: Platform Library ids the participant brings (airframe, UAV, ship, vehicle, ground station), declared before its radios. De-duplicated. An id naming a deleted platform is kept.

expected_updated_at.description: The updated_at last read, as returned. When present and not equal to the stored value the save is refused with PARTICIPANT_STALE. Omit it on a first save.

asset_phases.description: Asset id to the phase ids it is present in. Omit or send null to leave the stored rows alone: an asset newly added to the lists then goes into every phase, and an asset removed from them loses its rows. When sent, each key must be one of the check-in's own platform_ids, equipment_ids or transport_ids (PARTICIPANT_UNKNOWN_ASSET) and each phase id a phase of this operation (OPERATION_UNKNOWN_PHASE). An asset in the lists but missing from the map is placed in every phase; an empty list means brought, in no phase.

AdhocOrganization.description: An "Other" partner named only inside one operation. It is never added to the organization library.

branch.description: A branch or an alias such as Army, stored canonical. Blank for none.

UpdateParticipantRequest.description: Replaces the whole check-in addressed by id: all four lists and the contact fields are stored as sent, so an omitted list becomes empty.

platform_ids.description: Platform Library ids the participant brings (airframe, UAV, ship, vehicle, ground station), declared before its radios. De-duplicated. An id naming a deleted platform is kept.

expected_updated_at.description: The updated_at last read, as returned. When present and not equal to the stored value the save is refused with PARTICIPANT_STALE. Omit it on a first save.

asset_phases.description: Asset id to the phase ids it is present in. Omit or send null to leave the stored rows alone: an asset newly added to the lists then goes into every phase, and an asset removed from them loses its rows. When sent, each key must be one of the check-in's own platform_ids, equipment_ids or transport_ids (PARTICIPANT_UNKNOWN_ASSET) and each phase id a phase of this operation (OPERATION_UNKNOWN_PHASE). An asset in the lists but missing from the map is placed in every phase; an empty list means brought, in no phase.

CreateParticipantRequest.description: Names either a library organization or an ad hoc one, not both and not neither, plus what it brings. An omitted list is empty.

organization_key.description: A library organization's key. Omit when adhoc is sent.

platform_ids.description: Platform Library ids the participant brings (airframe, UAV, ship, vehicle, ground station), declared before its radios. De-duplicated. An id naming a deleted platform is kept.

asset_phases.description: Asset id to the phase ids it is present in. Omit or send null to leave the stored rows alone: an asset newly added to the lists then goes into every phase, and an asset removed from them loses its rows. When sent, each key must be one of the check-in's own platform_ids, equipment_ids or transport_ids (PARTICIPANT_UNKNOWN_ASSET) and each phase id a phase of this operation (OPERATION_UNKNOWN_PHASE). An asset in the lists but missing from the map is placed in every phase; an empty list means brought, in no phase.

position.description: Index in the operation's order, from 0.

supported_participant_id.description: The participant this phase supports, or null for none.

placements.description: Participant id to the id of the site it sits at in this phase. A participant absent from the map is not placed. Never null.

requirements.description: The pairs of participants that must be able to talk in this phase, ordered by a then b. Never null.

SavePhasesRequest.description: The operation's whole ordered phase list; positions are the array index.

id.description: A phase of this operation to keep, renamed or repositioned. Omit for a new phase.

name.description: Trimmed; unique within the request, case-insensitively.

a.description: A participant id, sorting before b.

RFICommentResponse.description: One reply in an RFI's flat thread.

created_by_id.description: Local user id of the replier.

RFIResponse.description: A request for information one unit raises to the others on an operation.

participant_id.description: The unit the RFI was raised as; null once that unit is removed from the operation.

created_by_id.description: Local user id of the poster; the only user who can resolve the RFI.

resolved_by.description: Display name of who resolved it; empty while open.

rfis.description: Open RFIs newest first, then resolved ones. Never null.

participant_id.description: The unit the RFI is raised as; must be checked in to this operation.

position.description: Index in the operation's order, from 0.

SaveSitesRequest.description: The operation's whole ordered site list; positions are the array index.

id.description: A site of this operation to keep, renamed or repositioned. Omit for a new site.

name.description: Trimmed; unique within the request, case-insensitively.

supported_participant_id.description: A participant of this operation, or null (or blank) for none (PARTICIPANT_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

placements.description: Participant id to site id. Each participant must be checked in to this operation (PARTICIPANT_NOT_FOUND) and each site one of its sites (OPERATION_UNKNOWN_SITE).

requirements.description: Pairs that must talk, in either order. A pair of one participant is refused (OPERATION_REQUIREMENT_SELF).
